title: M1.1: Channel binding records, owner routes and rollout switch
description:
Add the ChannelBinding item (tenant_id, binding_id, provider, route key, default bot, enabled, limits, created_by, created_at), the global route lookup item (route#provider#routeKey to tenant and binding, no content), the per-organization external_channels rollout switch plus per-environment kill switch, and owner-only HTTP routes under /orgs/{tenant}/channel-bindings (create, list, get, update, disable). Mirror the bot board access model: owners change, members read, strangers get 404, role read at every request. Add the organization mail_handle (lowercase DNS label, unique per environment, reserved words refused).

Acceptance criteria:
- An owner creates an email binding and gets the derived address bot AT mail_handle.mail-domain
- A member can list but not change; a member of another organization gets 404; a removed owner loses access at the next request
- Two organizations cannot claim the same route key or mail_handle
- With the rollout switch off the routes answer as if the feature does not exist for members
- Disabling a binding keeps its data and stops admission and delivery (asserted in later features)
- No schema migration; items use tenant_id keys

Gherkin: features/external_channel_binding.feature

Contract: the External channels contract (initiative description; draft docs/EXTERNAL_CHANNELS.draft.md).

Process: Gherkin first (AGENTS.md outside-in). Write the named feature, add it to features/cucumber-features.txt, implement steps in conversation/features-support/steps/, then production code. Vitest only for pure helpers. Both cucumber-js and vitest must pass. No emojis, no compatibility forks, tenant_id on every item, strangers get 404. Product PR into develop with sub-agent review.
